common_name: Audrey Hardy Kiwi (Male Pollinator for Natasha and Tatyana)

planting.note: Plant this male-only vine within pollinating range of female hardy kiwi selections such as 'Natasha' or 'Tatyana'; it bears no fruit of its own but supplies pollen with timing matched to those cultivars.

directions: Audrey is a male Actinidia arguta selection valued specifically for its above-average cold tolerance and bloom timing that overlaps the female cultivars 'Natasha' and 'Tatyana'. Like all hardy kiwi males, it never sets fruit itself but exists purely to supply pollen to nearby female vines, since the species is dioecious. Its hardiness makes it a useful pollen source for far-northern plantings where more tender male clones can suffer winter dieback. Train it on a sturdy trellis alongside the female vines it is meant to service, spacing it within normal pollination range.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female selection is noted for extra cold tolerance and is commonly paired with the male pollinator 'Audrey'.

directions: Natasha is a female Actinidia arguta selection noted among hardy kiwi growers for tolerating colder winters than many of the more commonly sold cultivars. It is typically paired with the male selection 'Audrey', whose bloom period is timed to overlap and ensure reliable fruit set. Like other hardy kiwiberries, it produces smooth-skinned, grape-sized fruit that can be eaten whole once ripe, skin and all. Give it a strong permanent trellis and full sun, since the twining vine becomes vigorous and heavy once established.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female selection shares the above-average cold hardiness of 'Natasha' and needs a separate male hardy kiwi such as 'Audrey' nearby for pollination.

directions: Tatyana is a female Actinidia arguta selection valued for above-average cold hardiness, often grown alongside the similarly hardy cultivar 'Natasha' in northern kiwiberry plantings. It requires a male pollinator such as 'Audrey' planted within range, since hardy kiwi vines are dioecious and will not set fruit from a female vine alone. The vine produces small, smooth-skinned fruit typical of the species, best harvested once fully soft and sweet. Provide a sturdy trellis and consistent moisture during the first few growing seasons to establish a strong root system.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female selection needs a separate male hardy kiwi vine nearby for pollination and produces distinctively red-blushed fruit.

directions: Scarlet September is a female Actinidia arguta selection grown for sweet, oval-shaped fruit that develops a distinctive red blush as it ripens in early autumn. As with other hardy kiwi cultivars, it is dioecious and needs a separate male vine growing nearby to produce a worthwhile crop. The red coloring sets its fruit apart visually from the more common green-fleshed hardy kiwi selections, though the flavor remains similarly sweet-tart. Train the vigorous twining vine on a permanent trellis in full sun and expect several years of establishment before significant fruiting begins.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female numbered selection needs a separate male hardy kiwi vine, such as '119-40B', planted nearby for pollination.

directions: 74-32 is a numbered female Actinidia arguta selection from the same Cornell hardy kiwi breeding trials that produced the related selections '74-46' and '74-49'. It is grown mainly by hardy kiwi collectors and specialty fruit nurseries interested in diversifying plantings beyond the handful of widely sold commercial cultivars. As a dioecious vine it will not fruit without a compatible male hardy kiwi growing within pollinating distance. Provide a sturdy, permanent trellis, since established vines become heavy and vigorous over time.

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female numbered selection is a sibling of '74-32' and '74-49' and needs a separate male hardy kiwi vine nearby for pollination.

directions: 74-46 is a numbered female Actinidia arguta selection originating from the same Cornell hardy kiwi breeding trials that also produced '74-32' and '74-49'. Specialty fruit nurseries distribute it mainly to collectors assembling diverse hardy kiwiberry plantings rather than as a single standout commercial variety. Fruit set depends on a nearby male Actinidia arguta vine, since the species is dioecious and female selections cannot pollinate themselves. Like its sibling selections, it needs a sturdy permanent trellis and several years to reach full production once transplanted.

common_name: Emerald Arctic Beauty Kiwi (Large-Fruited Kolomikta Kiwi)

planting.note: Plant on a trellis or fence in full sun; this female selection needs a male Actinidia kolomikta pollinator, such as 'Pasha' or 'Adam', growing nearby to set fruit.

directions: Emerald is a trademarked female Actinidia kolomikta selection bred for unusually large, sweet, lime-green fruit compared with older kolomikta cultivars. It needs a male Actinidia kolomikta pollinator, such as 'Pasha' or 'Adam', planted nearby to set its crop, since the species is dioecious. Unlike many ornamental kolomikta selections grown mainly for variegated foliage, Emerald is marketed specifically for its fruiting performance. Give it a trellis or fence to climb and full sun for the best fruit flavor and foliage color.
